analysis: Pseudotumour cerebri, also known as idiopathic intracranial hypertension, is a condition characterized by increased intracranial pressure without an identifiable cause. Among the listed drugs, Tetracycline is well-documented to be associated with this condition due to its potential to increase intracranial pressure. The other options, Sparfloxacin, Gentamicin, and Clofazimine, do not have a recognized link to Pseudotumour cerebri in the medical literature. While Clofazimine has been mentioned in broader discussions, it lacks a direct causal relationship with the condition. Therefore, based on established pharmacological knowledge, Tetracycline is the most relevant and supported option for causing Pseudotumour cerebri.
